candidate.title: MALBAC
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina MALBAC (Multiple Annealing and Looping-Based Amplification Cycles) genomic-DNA amplification schematic, interpreted against the primary 2012 MALBAC WGA description. The depicted component begins with genome plus MALBAC primers, retains genomic-template and partial-amplicon routes through repeated quasilinear amplification and intramolecular full-amplicon looping, and ends at common-sequence PCR-amplified DNA. It does not depict downstream fragmentation, sequencing-adapter installation, sequencing or computational analysis. No version, product kit implementation or unshown cDNA/RC-seq/DR-Seq adaptation is added to the target.

states.label: Genomic DNA template
features: Starting material is genomic DNA (Genome). The primary figure caption resolves the accessible annealing substrate as single-stranded genomic DNA after melting; that upstream melting operation is not separately drawn here.
The target is the genome, including sequence variation and regional DNA copy number; no RNA branch is depicted.

operations.label: Cycles of quasilinear amplification
operations.description: The circular route repeats the depicted Hybridize primers, Synthesis and Denature steps. Within this shared reaction, partial amplicons are copied into full amplicons with complementary ends, while retained genomic DNA generates additional partial amplicons. Full-amplicon ends hybridize within the same molecule to form the depicted Looped full amplicons, suppressing their further use as templates during these cycles. Partial amplicons and genomic template remain eligible for subsequent rounds. These are coexisting molecular classes in one reaction, not separately isolated branches. Repetition and the template-return route are represented within this operation.
operations.mechanism: Repeated random primer annealing, strand-displacing synthesis and strand separation; intramolecular hybridization between complementary 3′ and 5′ ends sequesters completed full amplicons during preamplification. Looping is end annealing, not covalent circularization.
operations.information_effect: Genomic sequence is carried by amplified DNA inserts. Loop-based exclusion reduces repeated copying of completed products and associated bias, without ensuring complete or unbiased genome representation.

evidence.locator: b00012, comparison of MALBAC and DR-Seq coverage bias
evidence.quote: Both DR-Seq and MALBAC, relying on quasilinear amplification using random primers to amplify the genome, display greater coverage biases than bulk sequencing but perform similar to each other (Fig. 2g).
evidence.rationale: Full-text comparison supports the limitation that quasilinear amplification still has coverage bias; it does not establish an extra target workflow for this diagram.

operations.label: PCR
operations.description: Exponentially amplify the full-amplicon population after quasilinear preamplification, yielding the final DNA products.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper specifies PCR primers matching the common 27-nucleotide sequence. Looping suppression applies to preamplification; the full amplicons can subsequently serve in PCR.
operations.information_effect: The amplified genomic inserts are the physical carrier of sequence information from the starting genome. Subsequent sequencing can support copy-number inference from genomic coverage and nucleotide-variant assessment from base identities. The schematic draws neither sequencing nor analysis. Amplification can lose regions or alleles and propagate early polymerase errors, so these products do not themselves guarantee complete genome recovery or error-free single-cell variant calls.

method_scopes.rationale: MALBAC (Multiple Annealing and Looping-Based Amplification Cycles) is the sole target: the card title, the image label beside Genome, and the collection page heading and caption agree. All five operation instances apply to this genomic-DNA amplification component. The repeated block explicitly contains both partial-amplicon→full-amplicon and retained-genome→additional-partial-amplicon routes, with looping within the repeats; they are molecular classes in a common reaction. The 2012 primary paper supports this architecture. The collection page mentions cDNA applicability in prose, and the card cites DR-Seq and other applications, but the assigned drawing shows no transcriptome branch or alternative method. No complete downstream sequencing-library implementation or equivalence to those applications is asserted.
